A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VideoCoF research, with readable methods, equations, figures, tables and complete supplementary material. Retained content can be matched across appendix renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original VideoCoF-Bench experiments, qualitative editing examples and ablations of reasoning frames, RoPE and prompting.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds TGVE+, V2VBench and longer-video evaluation results.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 adds a reported accelerated inference option using DMD-LoRA with four steps. The underlying Chain-of-Frames construction, RoPE design, training objective and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that the retained benchmark scores use this acceleration.

E1.justification: v2 adds standalone evaluations on TGVE+ and V2VBench in supplementary Section 9, substantially broadening evaluation beyond VideoCoF-Bench. TGVE+ covers 1,417 samples across seven editing tasks. The existing training data and VideoCoF-Bench coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds TokenFlow alongside the five retained baselines, and Figure 10 compares against a baseline augmented with UltraViCo. New benchmark comparisons additionally include Tune-A-Video, SDEdit, STDF, Fairy, EVE, SimDA, VidToMe, VideoComposer and MotionDirector, substantially expanding the comparator families.

E3.justification: The added TGVE+ evaluation specifies a 1,417-sample subset and reports PickScore, CLIP-F and two ViCLIP metrics; V2VBench introduces seven quality, consistency and alignment metrics. New extrapolation tests reach approximately 512–513 frames in single-shot and multi-shot settings. Existing VideoCoF-Bench protocols and the 33-frame training setup are retained.

E4.justification: New supplementary Sections 6–7 add targeted qualitative analyses of UltraViCo's failure to solve the baseline's extrapolation problem and VideoCoF's degradation during long multi-shot editing. The existing RoPE, reasoning-format, reasoning-length and prompting ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added tables continue reporting point estimates without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Matched existing scores are unchanged, including Table 1's 8.97 instruction-following score and 76.36% success ratio for VideoCoF. v2 adds TokenFlow results, TGVE+ results including 20.90 PickScore and 0.956 CLIP-F, and V2VBench results including 5.024 frame quality. It also reports approximately 10-second accelerated inference and degradation near frame 512. These are additional results, not improvements over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: The latent definitions, Equations 1–2, RoPE index construction and training mathematics are retained. The added RoPE discussion provides qualitative explanations and comparisons rather than new formal definitions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The conclusion expands the stated length-extrapolation capability from four times the training length to up to sixteen times. The central claims about mask-free temporal reasoning, RoPE alignment and strong performance using 50k training pairs remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 removes the assertion of theoretically infinite extrapolation and documents a practical qualification: multi-shot editing degrades near frame 512 despite earlier stability. Supplementary Section 6 also explains how source-target alignment and index collisions distinguish this problem from repetition in text-to-video extrapolation.

D1.justification: v2 newly reports training on 16 H100 GPUs and four-step DMD-LoRA inference taking about 10 seconds for 33 frames on one H100. However, it removes v1's global batch size of 16, AdamW optimizer and learning rate of 1e-4. These omissions do not establish changed training settings. Existing data recipes, prompts and resource-access statements are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 broadens its citations across training-free, training-based and MLLM-guided editing. New supplementary discussion explicitly distinguishes VideoCoF from UNIC, RIFLEx and UltraViCo, while additional references support the new comparisons and acceleration. This extends the positioning without replacing the original research framing.

P1.justification: v2 adds VideoCoF to the title, updates authorship and correspondence information, and corrects grammar and terminology. The supplement gains three sections and renames Discussion to Future Directions, while most existing prose and its narrative order remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds two benchmark tables and two qualitative figures, inserts TokenFlow into Table 1, and reflows the supplement. Existing supplementary Figure 10 and Tables 4–7 are retained as Figure 12 and Tables 6–9. Main figures retain their visual content, with limited label and caption corrections.

improvement.justification: The added external benchmarks strengthen empirical support, and the documented extrapolation failure makes the account more credible than v1's infinite-extrapolation assertion. These gains outweigh a limited reproducibility regression from removing training hyperparameters, although sparse procedural detail for the new evaluations and DMD-LoRA limits the overall improvement.
